::: {.cell context='setup' autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
download.file(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emzou/r-guide/main/datasets/titanic.csv",
  "titanic.csv"
)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
df <- read_csv("titanic.csv")
```
:::




We just made a frequency table for `Survived`, whether or not a passenger survived the Titanic. 
Likewise, we can make a the class for Titanic passengers, which is indicated in `Pclass`. 



::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
df %>% count(Pclass)
```
:::




# Bar Plot
- A bar plot is the visual version of the frequency table. 
- We can show this result with a bar plot, using the ggplot() and geom_bar() function from the **ggplot2** package. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Pclass)) + 
  geom_bar()
```
:::




- This plot works when we only have *one* variable we're showing. 
- We specify which variable we are interested in within the aes() call, which in the above code, we put as "x = Pclass". 
- We can make the same plot for other variables by changing what we set x equal to. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Sex)) + geom_bar()
```
:::




## Improving Readability 
### Labels 
We can add labels to our axes and a title for our entire plot by additionally calling labs(). 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Pclass)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Passengers by class", 
        x = "Passenger class", 
        y = "Count") 
```
:::




### Themes
- ggplot comes with themes (you can peruse them [here](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggtheme.html)). 
- We can make our plot follow `theme_minimal()` by adding it. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Pclass)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Passengers by class", 
        x = "Passenger class", 
        y = "Count") + 
  theme_minimal()       
```
:::




### Fill 
We can also customize the color of the bar with geom_bar. 




::: {.cell autorun='false'}

```{.webr .cell-code}
ggplot(df, aes(x = Pclass)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Passengers by class", x = "Passenger class", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```
:::
